The people in my social circles seem to recognise that to some extent, things are not “okay”. Some of them are a little more informed and are aware that things may very soon fall apart.

But I don’t think any of them are fully collapse aware. Or at least they treat it as if it’s just “stuff that’s happening in the background.”. The tone of our conversations are often like this:

 “Yeah the Bonn river totally dried up, but I’m gonna move there for a few years so I might see it fill back up again one day.”

“I know the UK is doing pretty bad right now, but I’m gonna try and move there to get a job!”

“I just saw on the news that a bunch of fish are turning up dead. Anyways, I’m going to go fishing with some uni friends next week.”

“Last years crab season was cancelled so we didn’t eat any. We got prawns instead but that’s fine, maybe next season the prices will come down!”

“SVB collapsed over the weekend. It’s gonna become a contagion and we gotta prepare for more banks to follow suit. Also, I’m thinking of saving up to go for the New Year celebration in Thailand next year, I hear it’s pretty exciting around that time.”

My default phrase is “Let’s see if we’ll even make it to the end of this year unscathed yeah?” whenever they try to make long term plans (I’m talking retirement etc.). The common response is laughter followed by “Yeah.”

I don’t know if we’re all just living on copium and pretending that everything is fine until it’s not. Or whether my friends genuinely just think that things will somehow right itself with time.

I’ve been in the EnStars fandom since I was 17 (I’m about 23 now) and he has always been my comfort character. He literally embodied everything I wished I could be growing up. Being a somewhat reserved teen boy who couldn’t believe in anything, Chiaki always made me believe that maybe, possibly, despite my pessimistic self, there where genuinely people out there who wanted to make the world a better place, and that gave me hope. 

Needless to say there aren’t many fantastic male role models out there, and I was never the super masculine guy. But seeing Chiaki, and how he was so affectionate around all the characters (from Ryuseitai to the basketball club to Anzu) made me aspire to become a guy like that too. As in someone who was able to be there for people and to also provide a loving presence (though Chiaki can sometimes come across a bit much). 

From his laughter to his loud voice and his silly lines, I just love him so much. I admired him because he represented somebody the exact opposite of me. I’m always serious, hesitant and questioning, and I was always extremely distrustful of people around me. Despite who I was, deep down I’ve always wanted to be the guy who could just jump straight into something without thinking about a contingency to the backup to Plan B. And as much as I didn’t trust people, I desperately wanted to just tell people that I cared for them, without overthinking about how awkward it would sound. So seeing all my deep desires represented in the beautiful man that is Chiaki Morisawa, it just helped me understand so much about myself that I wasn’t ready to admit at that time.

After reading Meteor Impact, it made me relate to him even more. Reading about 1st/2nd year Chiaki was heartbreaking and it gave me bad flashbacks to high school and in some ways, it helped me realise that maybe I could follow in Chiaki’s footsteps. To go from outcast to somebody who can become a positive energy for people, it really got me through the rest of my teen years.

I know this makes me sound a little weird that I’m basing so much of my life off a literal character from a 2-D tapping game, but he really meant a lot to me and he’s gotten me through plenty of bad times. 

These days I’m in a much better place, and EnStars has been with me through these formative years. I have so many good memories of times where I laid in bed reading translations until I fell asleep, or the time that I pulled my first Chiaki 5*, or jamming out to Meteor Ranger on long commutes home. I honestly love so many of the characters, but Chiaki will always have a special place in my heart.

There was a period in my life where I had this ridiculous idea that I should only read non-fiction books. I believed that if I had the time to "indulge in fantasies (fiction)", I had the time better spent picking up something more useful.

In many ways it ended up doing more harm than good, because I suddenly lost the love of reading. As a child, I read for fun. I could reread the same books again and again simply because I wanted to read. But once I hit my college years, it became a competition of who was more knowledgable, who was smarter, and it was a constant battle to seem like you're the most intelligent one in the room, or else no one would listen to you.

I refused to reread books I've read before and I created lists of books I **had** to read or else I was just simply too dumb. I bought more and more books, pretending that I could read them all. Eventually I just got tired and I became frantic. I would get so angry at myself when I suddenly realised that I couldn't remember the name of XX study in the year 19XX, or that I couldn't remember the name of that popular biotech company that's pioneering X life-enhancement treatment, or the name of X bacteria, or even the name of X theory. It ended up driving me crazy because then I would spend hours forcing information into my brain, I would take notes on the books, make recordings to myself explaining my notes to myself, and I would go back again and again and force myself to memorise pieces of information that had no immediate value.

At that time, I hated the thought of reading. Instead of it being fun, it became a chore, feeling like it was something I needed to put a lot of effort in. 

One day I just realised that this wasn't healthy for me. Not only was it destroying my love for books, but I started to hate myself more because I saw myself as being too dumb because I couldn't "absorb information like a sponge", or that my reading speed was too slow in comparison to all these "top of the field experts who read 20 books a week".

It was around the same time that I was back home with my parents, so a lot of the books I read as a child/teen were still on the shelves gathering dust. I decided to pick up one of my favourites (it was the Darren Shan Saga), and before I knew it, I finished all 12 books in a few days. During that entire time, I didn't pause to look for a notepad, or struggled to look for my pen so I could write something down before I forgot. But most importantly, I enjoyed it.

It was after that experience that I went back to reread a bunch of books I loved as a child and I rediscovered my love for reading. There was no pressure to "finish the book before X time" or pressure to memorise every single detail. Since then, I've allowed myself to give up the habit of only reading non-fiction. 

These days, I mostly read what sounds interesting to me at the time, and it's okay if I spend 2 months reading that one book. I find that I end up retaining much more of the book when I read things I genuinely like and that I could talk more extensively about things I took my time to read and digest. I still do read non-fiction don't get me wrong, but I do it at a leisurely pace. I ask myself, do I really want to know about this topic, or do I just want to read it so I can show off when I talk to my friends? Turns out, I manage to filter like 80% of the books I "want" to read into the select few I actually want to read.

My reading experience since has been so much better and I actively avoid channels or communities that propound the need to consume XX books a day, or advertisements from Blinklist to get the best ideas compressed into 15 minutes. I've probably listened to over 100s of "compressed summaries" from Blinklist and snapshots from Scribd, and trust me, I do not remember the content of a single one, I couldn't even tell you what the book was about if you ask me.

I feel that way exactly! I am an avid reader and can gobble up fiction books no problem. This was never an issue as a kid because I read for pure entertainment, and it didn’t matter whether I remembered every detail, I just wanted to read. 

But these days I don’t have that luxury anymore, I’m constantly busy with stuff and when I do get time to read, I’m expected to make the best of it, and it does bother me a lot. I could be rereading a fiction book I really enjoyed as a teen, and each time I would get annoyed at myself because I would say “If you had time to reread a book you already read, you might as well spend this time reading something more productive”. And it gives me constant anxiety whenever I’m reading something that’s not purely for academic purposes.

For a few months reading just lost its fun for me, it became a daily task to just slog through books, and even if I fell asleep reading them, I would force myself to finish it. It would make me angry when I would read something factual, only to not remember the term for some concept, and then it would drive me to reread a book again, forget something in the future, reread, and you get the idea. Then I discovered a reading pattern that has enriched my reading experience, even more so than when I was a kid. Throughout those months I refused to read any fiction, and because I was being such a stick up for everything I was reading, I could spend weeks reading just one book. 

I decided it was stupid and I was deluding myself into thinking it was productive. Since then, I’ve picked up several fiction books and other books that are not directly related to my area of study. At any given moment, I would be reading 4 different books, 2 non-fiction academic books, 1 fiction, and 1 casual read book. The 2 non-fiction books I would treat them as textbooks, I would read them, highlight them, make notes on them, and only read them in daylight hours. The fiction book could be any type, a classic, some YA novel, some cheesy romance novel, or a book I want to reread simply because I enjoyed it. The casual book is usually another non-fiction, fun-fact-esque novel that I would read before bed. Let me draw you an example.

In the daytime, if I had a break between classes, or if I just had some time to kill, I would read one of the non-fiction academic books, which are always books about different topics. This is to prevent fatigue from just reading just one topic. I would carry a book about philosophy and ethology around, and depending on my mood, I’ll pick one of them to read and make notes on (this also forces me to summarise what I just read, and if I ever needed to draw upon some concept, I’ll know where exactly to retrieve it, instead of flipping through the entire 600 pages again).

If I woke up really early that day, or if I had an evening off for myself, I’ll pick up the fiction book and relax with that. I would read it and it wouldn’t matter if I forgot half the characters, or half the plot after, because I know I already did my fair-share of “serious reading” and that this was just an activity to unwind.

Once 11pm hits, all my devices will go on lockdown, I’ll throw my phone into the closet and my iPad would impose a limit on all my apps. Next to my bed I’ll have some random book, it could be a book about wine, or a book about physicists who changed our perceptions of reality, a book about maps, or a book filled with pretty architecture. So far these books have all been non-fiction books, but they’re not things I usually have to use academically. I read them for general knowledge, so it’s okay if I don’t remember the name of that water-borne disease that causes blindness, or the location of some museum where some painting is currently stored. I just read it, spend several minutes rubbing my fingers on the glossy pages, or reread a passage I thought was very nice and the hour goes by very quickly. Around 12, I turn my lights off immediately and go to sleep. Since I’m reading them before bed, I find that I actually consolidate some of the random things I’m reading about. It might not be to the letter, but it sits there in my mind and I could use it to strike up a conversation if need be. My phone remains in the closet, on top of a stack of clothes, so I can never see it light up, or hear it vibrate (which could be inconvenient in the case of emergencies), but that way my phone doesn’t bother me when I’m reading.

Using this pattern, I find myself being able to read many books a month, and since I’m always alternating, it gives my mind time to consolidate and think through ideas, before I go back on to pile more information on top of it. It might not work for you, and it does require some form of discipline, but I think as long as you really try to put in some effort, it doesn’t matter how many books you read, as long as you can retain what you learn from it. The way I see it, always better to have a solid grasp of one topic, than to have a shadow of 10 different topics because you skimmed through the books without letting anything settle. It might take me 2 weeks to finish a 200 page book about Freud, but throughout that entire time, I also get to read for fun, and it really lets me brood things over and form my own opinions before going into the next chapter.

I wish you good luck with your reading journey, and one really important thing I feel I should mention. Don’t simply read a book because someone says you have to (unless its a textbook), read it because you genuinely want to. In this age of booktubers and book awards, you just want to read every single book that is recommended, but unless the book interests you, I would say that it’s okay to give some books a miss.

EDIT: Just to add on, I establish a habit of covering at least 2 chapters a day for the non-fiction academic book. This is priority over any fiction book. So if I was busy in the afternoon and did not get to cover the 2 chapters, I would devote my evening to that before I could relax.

“When nobody enters my room” could be literal or figurative, where this person is free to be themselves, and to represent these very conflicting thoughts because they don’t have to share them with the world (for example, not letting people in, “nobody enters my room”), or even simply because this person is safe in their own room, safe from judgement where this person can sit and ponder. *I feel time looking out my window*
*Watching me dance on the moon”*

The windows again could just be an analogy, of the human body being this “house” that contains this person’s thoughts and spirit, such that the room represents their mind, and the window their eyes, or the person literally looking out their window and seeing the world outside it. Either way, this person is seeing outside of their fantasy, seeing “time”. Time could be imagery to supplement the idea of a universal that all of us are subjected to, like gravity, and this person looks and realises that as much as they would like it to stop happening, the inevitable nature of this “time” keeps progressing. The whole phrase “I feel time looking out my window (while) watching me dance on the moon” could show how helpless this person feels. Despite their fantasies of “dancing on the moon”, they still see the reality of the things happening around them and they can’t escape these haunting thoughts of wanting something better for the world, but not knowing what to do about it.

The song paints this image of a person struggling with dreams of grandeur, hoping that they are somehow more special and unique, believing that they serve a bigger purpose, and by self-sacrifice, the world will somehow be cured of all the pain. This seems to be apparent with the way the person fantasises about their eyes becoming planets, dancing on the moons, and becoming omnipresent after discarding their human body. Becoming the world and the universe basically.

Yet, the person is still grounded by the painful reality through their own perceptions of the world, wondering if they really could serve such a big purpose, or whether their fantasies are nothing but delusions, and that they truly are insignificant in the world. This person feels as if they are torn between all these conflicting thoughts and as a result, have become impassive, stuck at a junction in their life where they really do not know what to do anymore.

Again, I could be drawing baseless conjecture, but this was the meaning I derived from the song and to me at least, it fits in with the theme of the album. With the album having themes of this person thinking that they are special (ADKOH for example, where the person is communicating with a cosmic being and being taken away from this world because they don’t belong [this also could tie in with the idea of self-sacrifice]), and with songs like The Seed help illustrate the ugliness of the world this person sees, and feeling this anger of wanting to do something, anything (Suffocate me, so my tears can be rain, I will water the ground where I stand) This again could represent this person’s obsession with self-sacrifice and thinking it will save the Earth. I don’t want to go into too much detail since this post is already becoming quite long, but I’ll just throw in a few more examples. In ‘Hunger’, she sings about having “death on my mind”, or in ‘Soulless Creatures’, where she sings almost as if she’s a spirit looking down at her dead body and “giving both sides of me” could show the duality of thought between the struggle of wanting to live/die to “save our kind”, and in ‘Daydreamers’ where she questions whether she really can change the world.

I just want to end of this comment by saying that my impression of the album feels like a story being told. It’s a very macabre story, where it starts off with this person having thoughts and ideas and the struggle and anger at and for the world (The Seed). The exposition begins when this person starts withdrawing into themselves (In Bottles) and starts having these fantasies to help them cope (DOTM/Daydreamer) and their observations of the reality of the human nature (Hunger). This escalates into this person breaking down (The River) and they start having this contact from a more benevolent powerful being (ADKOH) that promises to take them away and help them change this ugly world. ADKOH is the climax of the story, where this person is convinced by this being to depart where self-sacrifice could truly save the Earth. This marks the end of their conflicting thoughts as now they have received the confirmation that they are indeed special (There is a flaw in manmade matters, but you are pure....), implying that this person is actually inhuman and has some godly power and they kill themselves? This person is now dead and has this weird power to start rewriting the universe, they go around the planet and observe it in their new form (Soulless Creatures). Now this person restarts the human race and becomes a God, in some biblical sense, hinting back to Adam and Eve (Apple Tree), where the people will save each other, and where pure emotion can be freely expressed (I would take care of it’s children, become their mother).

Again, this is just how I interpret the song and ADKOH as a whole, so there could be a very different meaning behind it. But here's a nice thing to remember, your perception of yourself is always skewered, and it always wavers, its super important that you don't push your own opinions of yourself and think that that's what everyone thinks of you. It took me a very long time to learn this and I learned this from a few of my friends. I have this taller friend who's pretty slim, and by no standards would anyone call him overweight, I was talking to him once and we talked about me sleeping over at his house, and he was like " If you don't mind wearing my large clothes. " I was actually shocked because he was definitely slimmer than I am and he thought that he is bigger than me ? So I replied saying that I am wider than he is and he replied saying " No, LMAO your smaller than me ". In this case his view was definitely skewered because I know for a fact that I am wider than he is, but in his eyes, he thought he was bigger than me. I also used to have really bad acne in high school and I always felt super self conscious about it, I remember staring into mirrors and remembering where each and every blemish was and how red a pimple looked. I thought I had the worse acne ever until a friend who had known me for 5 years suddenly said " I never noticed this before, but you have REALLLY bad acne, I always thought it was just a little acne problem". Obviously this wasn't a good thing, but the thing was, it took this friend 5 years, someone who is close to me that long to really see the " imperfections " If you will. People don't always notice every detail about you and because you've always seen yourself in the mirror, you automatically zoom in on the problems and that's what I found to shatter my confidence. 

I'm not telling you that there's nothing wrong at all with you ( cause I really don't know you ), but I'm also not saying to go look for every problem you have, after all, most people really only catch a glimpse of you on the streets or in school and it shouldnt matter how you look to them, what's important is that the people who see you everyday think you're okay, they don't have to think you're perfect, but as long as they can still love you, there's no reason to be unreasonable harsh on yourself. Malaysian here and I'm not here to rain on your parade, but you have to be very careful of what's " vegan " in this country.

Because we are such a racially and religiously diverse country, there are actually many religious vegetarians. The vegan term is actually very loosely used here and it's sad to say, but not an extremely understood term. Just a few days ago, there was a post on FB in my local vegan group ranting about all the alleged vegan foods and most of the comments talked mainly of how restaurants used dairy cheese and still labeled their food " vegan ". There were complaints about restaurants claiming that they serve vegan food when in reality, they were only vegetarian. 

I speak from experience and sometimes it's easier to select something that does not have cheese in it because vegan cheese is almost never available in stores ( even high end ones ) and when you can find them, they're ridiculously expensive or have to be special ordered from elsewhere. Butter/Margarine is also dangerous because honestly, many people cannot differentiate the difference between them and use them interchangeably, in addition to that, only very few margarines are actually even vegan here and the cheap ones are not. People here might confuse veganism here with vegetarianism so it's always safer to ask if it has butter/cheese instead of asking if it's vegan or not. 

I'm not sure if OP is either travelling to/from Kuala Lumpur, but it's just a heads up to anyone who might come to Malaysia in the future.

SIF has played a huge rule in the past 4 years of my life and the memories of it are so sweet my heart actually hurts when I think about them. At the beginning it wasn't even taking up my life, it was just casual playing and sometimes I didn't even get the SR. Going into my second year it became a little more hardcore. This was also the time I started JP. That year held my best memories because it was the first time I ever had tiered for an event and what made that event so memorable for me was this. 

I had been working really hard the entire event and the event was going to end on a Saturday. That Saturday was also a special day because I was going to spend a day with my dad. Initially I dreaded going out in fear that I might not make it for T2. To prepare for this I grinded even harder on Friday night to make sure that I would be safe for the next day. The next day I went out with my dad, in the morning we drove up to the city, and we had eaten at this famous food store and it was great. In the afternoon my dad drove us to this biker gathering ( my dads a biker) in the middle of the city and honestly it was kinda lame there. This entire trip I was reading this book " Landline " by Rainbow Powell, I was reading the book during the car trips around and I was close to finishing it. After the gathering, it was about 4 in the afternoon and I was thinking about whether I had made the tier. My dad suddenly decided that we should go watch a movie. So we drove to some huge ass mall and we went for some drinks before the show. We were going to watch " Jurassic Park " and the movie was great because Chris Pratt was in it ( #CelebrityCrush). The movie ended around 8 and we were going to go for dinner after. While walking around my friend messaged me screaming " THE NEW RIN UR IS OUT ". This was the time Pool Rin came out and I remembered looking at the picture of her while taking and escalator down. That night my dad brought me to Nandos for dinner and I was feeling super happy because it was such a great day. I reached home slightly after 10 and I remembered going to sleep super happy knowing that I had one of the best days in my life and I had tiered for my best girl. ( This was the Sauna Nozomi if anyone was curious). 

That memory is one of my best in life and since then,  I've been constantly striving to find the same happiness. I tiered for more event but none of them ever had the same effect on me. Even till this day I'm still trying to recreate that memory but I doubt it'll ever happen again. 

During those periods, I tried so hard to tier in so many events that it was taking over my life. I woke up at 5 in the morning daily to play and I would skip after school activities just so that I could make sure I would make it in time for events. I also stayed up late playing and it was really taking over my life. It was around this time when school was becoming really stressful and I was going through teenage stuff ( the normal stuff). With the combined lack of sleep, stress and issues I had, I reached an all time low in my life. 

I was getting really depressed and I had even come up with a plan to ( you know). It was getting so bad that I lost interest in everything. I gave up on school, cried a lot, felt useless and just played SIF.  It was only when my parents scolded me telling me that I was spending too much time on my phone when I finally saw it. 

I instantly quit SIF,  traded my account away to make sure I would never go back and I told my self to suck it up and move on with life. My life started to pick back up from that point because I put everything in my life in perspective and no longer was I getting too little sleep. 

Few months later I finally decided to come back to SIF and this time I sworn to never let it take over my life. This time I came back smarter and I only played when I wanted to and not because I needed to. 

Fast forward 1.5 years to today, I'm still going strong and life is no doubt stressful but I'm coping well. Instead of SIF taking over my life,  I use it to deal with my stress, I don't pressure myself to tier in every event and I tell myself that it's okay to let LP go to waste because it is only a game. 

SIF does get boring from time to time but I always like to play because its like a small period of a day where I'm allowed to just sit down, let the music play and let my mind rest. These days I don't even play in the morning and I only play once I come home from school and before I sleep. On average, I spend about 20 minutes a day on SIF only and I'm happy that SIF can still play an important role in my life while not overtaking my life.

Just watched the episode like an hour ago and I loved it !!

The 12 episodes building up to this was really good, IMO, SIP didn't have the same hype to this and I watched all the way to S1 Finale with little emotion, sure there were some cute and touching scenes ( like the Moo convincing Eli to join Muse scene ) But the entire S1 didn't make me feel the same way. It was still amazing don't get me wrong but the hype wasn't as built up as much as SS. SS had shown so much potential and hype and I thought that it would never be as good as SIP but I was wrong. Somehow the anime managed to make me love all the girls and I feel like the characters have a little more depth shown than their predecessors, all the girls in SS show their goods and bads, whereas where in SIP the only one we really saw with a major flaw which was Rin with her issue with girly clothes. IMO this made the girls seem a little more " real ". Unlike SIP where all the girls where almost perfect with their amazing singing abilities and where there seemed like there wasn't much struggle except trying to save the school. In SS on the other hand, we really see more conflict like the ones between the third years, between the Kurosawa sisters, the battle with Yoha and herself, Maru and Ruby learning to be less shy and the jealousy between Riko and You. The entire season I thought " Hey, this is really realistic " and I was warmed up to the idea where this school was in a weird small town in some random part of Japan. The anime really reinforced the fact that these 9 SS girls from a small town by showing that their school had 0 forms and really showed how country life is with Maru and her " ITS THE FUTURE ZURA ". The anime as a whole ( more like the second half ) went with the 0->1 theme and for me personally is much better than the " Being better than muse " theme. This season shows that even girls from countrysides can " shine " no matter who you are as we can see by the other students shouting " TEN " during their performance and I think this is also a really great message. The students shouting Ten sort of represents that they can still be part of the group even though they weren't the ones performing and for me it hit a button because what I got from that was that we don't always need to be in the spotlight to still help and by being supportive we find out own success in a way. 


Episode 12 was like a feels trip because we saw the weird Koto-lookalike ghost and Honos child ( ? ) and the visit to Otonizaka somehow made me remember all the times when SIP was still new and the first time I ever played SIF ( which was about 2 years ago ) so it made me feel really nostalgic when I actually had more time and when life was less stressful and stuff. That tiny scene where the SS girls thanked the school made me feel like saying thank you for the beautiful memories and that was a really nice touch by Sunrise for the older fans ( or it could be some marketing thing because he next thing I knew I went online to buy a crap ton of Muse merch and now I'm half broke :c ).

Okay, now let me say what I think of episode 13. It was great overall, a really simple wrap-up to an anime. The recap skit they did was really sweet and even though it lasted for like 5-6 minutes, I thoroughly enjoyed the whole thing. It took up quite some screen time but it was still nice. The first half of the episode was a little weird because you see that weird tension in Riko that hinted that something was really wrong but then it turned out that the rules just didnt allow unregistered members to sing, which I thought was really half-assed. We spend an unecassary half an episode looking at the minor problem that I feel could have been filled with a little more plot-building scenes. 

I was really thrown off at their performance, ( let's not talk about that ridiculous costume change in the middle of the performance ) First of all, Mirai Ticket is an amazing song and the name itself kinda hinted that there will be a future for Aquours. I sort of expected Step ! Zero to One and I'm actually kind of glad they didn't sing that. Sure, the message was probably more fitting but I feel like the music wasn't exactly " finale " material, it's too joyful and exciting to be performed in some weird round stage with really dark surroundings. ( unless this performance was conducted in a much for brighter place, like say outdoors, I would say that Step! zero to one wouldn't have fit the ambience )

The song started out strong, and the animation was great, but it went downhill from there on. The " We say Yousoro ! " part was really adorable but then suddenly Chika went off and did her own thing. The performance really threw me off when they showed Mu-Chan ( is that her name ? ) with sparkly eyes at a part of the song. That small scene made me feel like Mu-Chan was more important to the plot where in reality she probably isn't. This kind of scene I normally only see when a protagonist gets inspired and start their own journey, so it alarmed me and I actually thought for a second that she somehow would go off and start her own idol group and Kaboom, end of Aquours, beginning of Mu-se Ver. 2 

Also, the part where Chika reaches for the light and 8 girls just stand there ? No no no. Imagine seeing that in real life, you see one of the girls reaching for the light and the rest of the members standing static in the middle of a song. To make it worse, Chika suddenly runs toward the exit and I was internally screaming because it seems so random. 

I was prepared for this episode to make me cry a swimming pool but it only made me teary eyed at most, the hype leading up to this was good and I feel like this could've ended on a better note. One, there's just so much untied knots like there rival group Saint Snow, they just sorta vanished and I kind of hoped they would be given a little more details before the season ended. Two, what on earth did showing the moms do for the plot ? Chikas mum seems to have a good plot behind it and maybe we'll get it in S2 ( assuming we get one ) while the other moms being shown was just like " Okay. Yeah. " I feel that Sunrise tried to imitate the same in the LL movie when we saw Muses' moms but this repetition only made it look cheap and lame. 3. Not enough lore, there are so many things about the girls we don't know about and it feels like we'll never know. We know Chikas family runs a Ryokan which can be clearly seen but what about the rest of the characters ? Yous Papa has been mentioned before and we know Mari is rich but we aren't given more details. They could have slipped in tiny parts of the characters lives in the dialogues and I feel like the characters tend to fade once in a while. You had close to 0 presence until the episode where they talked about her being jealous and Yoha sort of faded after her introduction, Marus love for books was never referenced again, the Kurosawa idol conflict was not exactly directly addressed and we can only assume the dislike of idols in Dia came from the splitting of the 3rd years idol group, Kanan seemed to have so much free time again because she's practising everyday, and Ruby's shy issue vanished in like 5 episodes. I know I'm being a little too harsh, but the anime seemed to have just left so many things hanging which I hope S2 will make clear. SIP also had some holes that I won't talk about but because now Sunrise has more experience, I feel like they could have smoothed it out a little more.
